target_customer: Direct to consumer ecommerce brands running paid social, email and SMS campaigns
problem: Traditional landing pages cost too much money and time to build, so brands cannot test enough variants. Viddy built landing pages around video so they could be made in under 20 minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS with Viddy building the first pages for customers
product_category: Video landing pages and shoppable video storefronts for ecommerce

founders.name: Harris Gani
founders.background_notes: Product and engineering background. His Mux team page identifies him as co-founder of Viddy.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video hosting and page templating are available off the shelf, so a two person team could build the product with ordinary web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Several shoppable video tools existed around this period and a landing page layer on top of video was easy to copy. The one differentiator was a done for you service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move specific to Viddy was found. YC lists the company as acquired but no buyer is public in the sources found.

market_need_then: Ecommerce brands were spending heavily on paid social and wanted more landing page tests. The company's own claim is a 15 to 30 percent conversion lift, unverified.

branding.domain_note: Used viddyapp.io rather than an exact match .com, and that domain now redirects to an unrelated site.

brand_strength.rationale: The name collides with the well known 2012 Viddy video app, which dominates search results. No press about the brand itself or community was found.

pivots.to: Video storefronts that convert paid social traffic better than Shopify
pivots.why: The launch post reframed the product as e-commerce video storefronts. Reason not stated beyond positioning.

outcome_analysis: Viddy was a two person team selling video landing pages to ecommerce brands, with a Postscript SMS integration as its visible distribution. YC lists it as acquired, but the buyer, date and price are not public in the sources found, so the cause and quality of the outcome cannot be judged.
notes: Funding of about 500K from YC and Bossa Invest appears only on aggregators (VCBacked, Village, FundedIQ) and is unverified, so no round is recorded. No dated competitor sources from the batch period were found. No acquirer found. Harris Gani appears on Mux's team page, which does not confirm an acquisition by Mux. Company website viddyapp.io now redirects to an unrelated domain and was not followed. Do not confuse with the 2012 Viddy video app acquired by Fullscreen in 2014.
